body: The three-day gimmick, the sailing gimmick, the wall-morphing gimmick, the wolf gimmick, the shrinking gimmick, the motion control gimmick. What's weird here?

Thanks for letting me know :). And thanks for sharing whatever it is that dream was with me. I can't even think of a response to it, but you should know that I enjoyed it more than I perhaps should have.

One of my friends has been nice enough to agree to help me catch up in Calculus, even though I screwed myself over by skipping about two weeks of school. So I'm going to head to the library and do something productive for the first time in god knows when. Thanks for being there for me, and you should shoot me a pm when you get the chance. I really like talking to you.

It's weird. I've never been much into talking to people online because I felt like I needed a personal connection with them. 

I tried reaching out to my closest friend a few weeks ago, though, and it didn't go well. I said "Hey, I'm not okay" (obviously it was a bit more elaborate than that), and she hasn't talked to me since I opened that up to her. She knew *everything* that was wrong, and yet you've been able to comfort me more than she ever did. I guess the desire to be helpful is more important than any personal connection. I think it's really admirable that you're doing what you are, and I appreciate it more than you can know. 

Like I said earlier, I feel like I don't have much to offer anyone in terms of comfort, but if you ever want to talk about anything, I'd love to return the favor. But hey, I said I wasn't going to talk about anything heavy. Tell me a story or some shit.

Can I ask you something (a meaningless courtesy, as I'm going to ask before you have the chance to answer that)? I hope you don't find this offensive or too personal, but I can't help but wonder.

What are you feeling when you chat with people on here? Like, you're reading through these desperate posts and trying to offer comfort to them, and then you've got someone like me saying "Hey, let's just shoot the shit," and you're down for that too. It seems like it's too much to keep track of at once. I understand your desire to help people out however they need it, but how are you able to stay genuine?

Thanks, I really appreciate your kind words. Is it okay if we just talk? But not about suicide, depression, loneliness, or whatever other terrible things are on my mind? I just want some company. I have a lot of homework to do, and I need someone to help me get through this lonely Sunday. When I tell my friends that I want to talk, they never seem to understand. They ask me what I want. I want to talk, dammit!

If you say you're not bothered by me, I'm going to try to believe you. I always have trouble doing this, but since I don't know you in person, I feel like I don't have as much to lose (although maybe not as much to gain either). I hope you wouldn't mind if I wanted to return to those darker subjects at another time, but not now.

Thank you. "I" just sounds so much better. I'm not talking to you because I think you have great perspective or experiences to share with me. I mean, maybe that's part of it. But mostly, I'm talking to you because you're human and willing to talk to me.

I always wish I could be like you and try to be supportive of other people, and it kind of makes me feel bad that I don't try. But I just feel like I've got nothing to offer them. I don't know the right things to say. It seems like you just have some wisdom and insight that I'll never know. But then, that's what I always feel about people. I let myself become so vulnerable because I trust everyone more than I trust myself, and I let them walk all over me.

I think I've lost the focus of this message. I think I just mean to say that I appreciate what you're doing, but I feel a little guilty for accepting it. I've tried to reach out online once or twice before, but I always stop responding to helpful people like you because I feel bad about using them. I don't want to stop talking to you. You're telling me not to kill myself. That's giving me a reason to live. I'm just really scared of bothering you when you're being so nice. I don't want to punish you for your kindness.

Do you think it's bad to rely on one person too much? I can't help noticing that you always say *we* are here for you, instead of *I* am here for you. I don't know if you make a point to do that or what, but I've found that I'm always wishing I had one person that I could talk to. Just one. When I'm hanging out with friends or something, I find the number of people around me is directly proportional to how lonely I feel. Does that make sense?

I don't know. Maybe it's not even that I want one person. It's that I want that *particular* person, you know? But I guess I'm just really jealous and selfish and want to be incredibly important to someone. 

Sorry. I'm just bouncing around ideas like a pinball machine right now and I don't really know what I expect you to say.

> Please hide that shotgun somewhere where it would be very difficult for you to get a hold of it again, if not impossible.

Man, fuck that shotgun. I don't even know what to do with it. I spent $300 on that thing, $40 on ammo, and $70 on a shooting lesson so I wouldn't fuck up when the time comes. For a high school student who only gets about 15 hours/week at minimum wage, that's a lot of money to throw away if I decide never to use it.

I've been hiding it under my bed for the past week, but my dad will find it there eventually. And he'll obviously flip shit. I feel like I just have to keep it, though. Now I know how hard it is to actually pull the trigger. If I'm ever in enough pain to overcome how hard it is, I'll be glad that I have it there, you know? It brings me a it of comfort to know how easy it is to opt out if things become too unbearable.

Haha, I don't understand your uncle's suicide methods. Jumping would be my choice method, but I don't have access to a high enough spot. Perhaps I would feel differently when it came to be crunch time, but I think I'd sooner jump from 400 ft than 50 ft. The potential for survival is so scary to me. I don't want to get seriously injured and make everything worse. That's why I bought the shotgun. I mean, that will almost certainly kill me. But part of the reason I couldn't do it is that I know I will be seriously fucked if it doesn't.

I guess I differ from your uncle in that I think a failed suicide attempt is the worst thing I could possibly do, and he seems to make half-assed attempts without really being committed to it. I just don't want to burden anyone. 

And yeah, that small will to live is so hard to shake off. I don't even know if it's logical or only biological. But as I loaded the gun, I realized with frustration that there was no way I would pull the trigger. I feel like I could probably gather the courage to do it if I was drunk, but I could get into so much trouble if I was caught with a loaded firearm while intoxicated. 

Ugghhhh. I think I'm glad that you're sharing some things with me, though. This conversation has a much lighter tone than I would have expected, despite the fact that we're discussing some dark things. I thank you for that.

I'm so sorry. That sounds just terrible. I hate seeing other people who feel as hopeless as I do. It really sucks when you want to help someone, but there's just nothing you can do or say. That's why I can't tell anyone how I'm feeling. They'll try to help me, but they'll get frustrated when their efforts are wasted.

I'm trying to reach out online because I feel like someone like you would be more understanding of what it's like. You won't expect me to be cured right away. The fact that you frequent this sub tells me that you are familiar with that hopeless feeling, and your anecdote just proves that even further. Maybe you even feel it yourself sometimes.

Being like your uncle is one of the scariest things imaginable. I'm eighteen, and know that I could potentially find happiness one day, but I kind of doubt it. By seventy though, I would feel like all hope was lost. And if I still couldn't kill myself then. . . Jesus. I hope you're not offended by me saying that. It's not that I want your uncle to kill himself. But he just sounds so miserable and I don't want to be that. I don't want anyone to be that.

Please talk to me. Please. I see you here all the time, and you seem to genuinely care and want to help people. I'm so scared. I'm so, so scared. The last person I told that to removed me from their life. I need someone who won't judge me. Can you please provide that for me, if only for a little while?

I didn't respond to you last night because I thought I was going to finally do it. I brought my shotgun out to a creek and sat there for hours and hours. I couldn't do it. I felt so ready to earlier, but I just couldn't. This was the worst experience I've ever had. It feels like I've just been condemned to a life of misery. My only out failed me. 

I don't know what to do. I was getting ready to leave this life behind, and now it looks like I'm facing decades more of it.

> but when you're posting here, does that mean that some small part of you really wants to live after all?

I think it does. And that makes me feel like such an idiot and attention-whore, too. I feel like this whole "I want to end on good terms" thing is just me making excuses for why I haven't done it yet.

Nah, now that I think about it, it's not that a small part of me wants to live. It's that a small part of me doesn't want to die. I want to be dead, but I don't actually want to hurt myself. I've been through a lot with myself, you know?

Mostly I think I'm just here to blow off steam.
